senses: a person who dupes another
Having a vibe; atmospheric and trendy.
Having positive vibes.
examples: Couples were dancing to the latest vibey music.

senses: A tough, short-napped material used for making overcoats.
ety: From Melton Mowbray, where this material was made.

senses: Not sterilized.
In Hinduism and Buddhism, a great teacher; a supremely wise guide.
In Sikhism, God.
ety: From Sanskrit सत्गुरू (satgurū), from सत् (sat, “true”) + गुरु (guru, “teacher”).

senses: A long, narrow strip of timber bent and bolted longitudinally to the ribs of a vessel, to hold them in position and give rigidity to the framework.
Synonym of launderette (UK)
examples: The laundrette was a decent walk away; the air outside its doors was always scolding and brash, as if the air there was so clean it could sting you.

senses: A circular saw.
One who attacks violently and/or mindlessly.
examples: Agriculture Secretary Edward T. Schafer is preparing to walk into a buzzsaw of criticism over American biofuels policy when he meets with world leaders to discuss the global food crisis next week.
So he keeps away from the intellectual buzzsaws; and, as both philology and philosophy grow ever more and more technical, the gap between them, if anything, widens.
Apparently the jay was unaware that the hawk no longer had its hold because it became a buzzsaw of blue fury, slashing the hawk several more times.

senses: A tune that keeps replaying in one's head or that one keeps thinking about, especially if unwanted.
ety: From ear + worm; senses 1 and 3 (“tune that keeps replaying in one’s head”; “earwig”) are a calque of German Ohrwurm (“tune that pops up in one’s memory all the time; earwig”) (from the idea of a creature burrowing into the ear, an erroneous belief where earwigs are concerned), while sense 2 (“moth larva”) refers to the fact that these pests infest, among other things, ears of maize or sweet corn.

senses: A sheet, a piece of cloth cut and finished as bedlinen.
ety: From Middle English bedeschette, bedshete, bed shete, equivalent to bed + sheet.

senses: The act of resorbing.
The redissolving, wholly or in part, in the molten magma of an igneous rock, of crystals previously formed.
The creation, principles, or ideals of abstractions, in particular art.
The presentation of ideas in an abstract manner.
A climbing leguminous plant of Southeast Asia and the southwest Pacific Islands, Derris elliptica, whose roots are a source of rotenone.
ety: From New Latin and translingual Derris, from Ancient Greek δέρρις (dérrhis, “leather, skin”), referring to the leathery pods, from δέρω (dérō, “I skin, I flay”).

senses: Any of several toxic antibiotics, derived from the soil bacterium Bacillus polymyxa, used to treat infections by gram-negative bacteria
ety: From translingual polymyxa + -in, from Bacillus polymyxa, from which the antibiotic was isolated.

senses: A free peasant (as opposed to a serf) of the lowest rank, below an earl and a thane; a freeman; also (more generally), a person without royal or noble status; a commoner.
A bondman or serf.
A freedman, ranked below a thane but above a thrall.
ety: Inherited from West Midland Middle English churle (“person not of the nobility or clergy; serf, servant, simpleton, fellow”, East Midland Middle English cherl), from Old English ċeorl (“freeman ranking below a þegn but above a thrall; commoner, peasant; countryman, husbandman; man; husband”), from Proto-West Germanic *kerl, from Proto-Germanic *karilaz (“elder; man”), from Proto-Indo-European *ǵerh₂- (“to grow old; to mature”). senses: A person who salvages and consumes food that has been discarded, especially one who wishes to protect the environment and challenge consumerism by means of waste reduction.
Something which fizzes.
A party or social gathering which turns out to be a disappointment.
examples: It's probably for the best you didn't come to the birthday party on Saturday: it was a fizzer.

senses: The performance of magic tricks.
The theory of dealing with illusions.
The doctrine that the material world is an illusion.
The use of illusionary effects in sculpture and art.
The act or process of extricating or disentangling; a freeing from perplexities; disentanglement.
The act of sending out or evolving.
A light splashing sound.
ety: Onomatopoeic. Connected with splash and splosh.

senses: A marsupial of several families of the order Diprotodontia, found in Australia and neighboring islands.
An opossum, a marsupial of the family Didelphidae of the Americas.
Originating in the heart.
Resulting from a disorder of the heart.
A short cloak worn around the shoulders, adopted as part of the uniform of various religious orders, later often with an embroidered image of a saint.
A bandage passing over the shoulder to support it, or to retain another bandage in place.

A devotional object, typically consisting of two rectangular pieces of cloth (often with an embroidered image or text) joined with cloth bands and worn with one piece over the chest and one in the back.
ety: From Middle English scapelar, from Latin scapulāre, from Latin scapula (“shoulder”). Compare scapulary.

senses: To free something from entanglement; to extricate or unknot.
To unravel; to separate into discrete components or units.
To become free or untangled.
examples: I had to disentangle him from his own shoelaces.
This overlapping is reflective of hybrid languages, where certain features (phonetic, orthographic, semantic, syntactic) are also difficult to disentangle.

senses: Of a vehicle: to collide with a bridge; to perform a bridge strike.
ety: From Storrow Drive in Boston, Massachusetts, a parkway containing multiple low-clearance bridges which are infamous for being struck by moving vans as college students move into the city. This parkway is in turn named for businessman James J. Storrow, whose widow Helen opposed its construction.
examples: The most amusing thing on our trip to the dentist was watching a truck storrow beneath a low bridge and get shaved like a tin can.

senses: meek, gentle, gentlemanly, upstanding, innocent
ety: From Hindi शरीफ़ (śarīf)/Urdu شریف, from Arabic شَرِيف (šarīf).

senses: A fast undertaken at the door of an offender, especially a debtor.
Within a group of individuals of the same sex.
Rice cake from the Philippines made from glutinous rice cooked in coconut milk, usually eaten sprinkled with sugar or laden with latik.
Predicated, stated.
ety: From Middle English predicat(e), from Old French predicat (French prédicat), from Medieval Latin praedicātum (“thing said of a subject, predicate”), substantivized from the nominative neuter singular of praedicātus, the perfect passive participle praedicō (“to proclaim”), see -ate (noun-forming suffix); see also Etymology 2 below. The adjective was derived from the noun by metanalysis, see -ate (adjective-forming suffix).

senses: A congenital idiot.
Having or using the layout of a French/Francophone keyboard.
ety: From the first six letters on the top row of the standard French keyboard.

senses: The liquor remaining after halite (common salt) has been harvested from saline water (brine).
The saline substance added to soy milk to coagulate it as a primary step in the production of tofu.
ety: From bitter with an unclear suffix, perhaps a dialect form of -ing.

senses: Someone who crosses; agent noun of cross
A scientist who studies glaciers.
examples: To most people, the huge ice sheets of Antarctica and Greenland are merely water that once was snow. To glaciologists and climatologists, they are storehouses of the Earth's former atmospheres.

A spike, protruding from the nose cone of a missile, designed to decrease supersonic drag.
One who advances or puts forward.
The overcaller's partner, especially one who bids following the overcall.
A second branch of a buck's antler.

Describing an ethnic group that has a distinct culture.
